objective: Determine whether task-selected causal subspaces retain effective and protected behavior across recurrent depths.
context: Exact Sudoku, ARC-style transformations and hidden-ending storyworld interfaces; development-depth steering, later-depth evaluation, physical metric and full normalized observer. Native checkpoints and official task data are separate resources.

steps.name: Define the public task
steps.description: Separate observation, allowed action, exact result and hidden evaluator data.

steps.name: Observe recurrent state
steps.description: Specify physical coordinates, metric, loop depth and H/L commit semantics.

steps.name: Fit candidate steering
steps.description: Use development states to select task-relevant causal directions.

steps.name: Construct matched nulls
steps.description: Match task Jacobian, signed intervention and dose while checking protected readouts.

steps.name: Test unseen depths
steps.description: Freeze selection and compare at later loops and disjoint task structures.

steps.name: Evaluate claim
steps.description: Separate exact task verification from causal efficacy and native-model generalization.

specific_questions.prompt: Construct a two-dimensional recurrent rotation in which a direction effective at one depth is ineffective at a later depth; compute the transported perturbation.
Give a finite example with target and protected readouts. Derive a permissible intervention and a norm-matched sham.
Explain why matching a raw linear projection may fail after nonlinear normalization; provide a numerical example.
Specify how official ARC inputs, synthetic transformations and development-depth selection should be separated to avoid leakage.

native_verifier: depth_steering_gym audit, exact task worlds and protected causal-subspace evaluator; native TRM bridge separate.
